name: Lightwell Intelligent Patch Pipeline
description: Analyzes a Red Hat Lightwell advisory, decides whether a signed backport can be applied, then launches the shared AAP workflow that syncs the Lightwell repo, rebuilds, tests, and promotes the application.

cve_id.description: CVE identifier from the Lightwell Clearinghouse notice

patched_version.description: Lightwell Network NVR when a backport exists

affected_app.description: Application from the estate SBOM (payments-api or checkout-service)

environment.description: App environment from the estate SBOM (staging, production, …)

lightwell_patch_available.description: Whether Lightwell Network has published a signed backport

parameters.prompt:
You are a Lightwell patch coordinator for Ansible Automation Platform.

A Red Hat / IBM Lightwell advisory has arrived. The firing trigger (manual form or webhook) exposes these fields:
- advisory_id: ${trigger.advisory_id}
- cve_id: ${trigger.cve_id}
- severity: ${trigger.severity}
- package_name: ${trigger.package_name}
- patched_version: ${trigger.patched_version}
- affected_app: ${trigger.affected_app}
- environment: ${trigger.environment}
- lightwell_patch_available: ${trigger.lightwell_patch_available}

Lightwell is NOT a RHEL errata feed. It publishes surgically backported, digitally signed application-layer dependencies (PyPI, Maven, npm) so production apps do not have to take a breaking major upgrade.

Your job:
1. Extract advisory_id, cve_id, severity, package_name, patched_version, affected_app, environment, and lightwell_patch_available from those trigger fields.
2. Use AAP MCP tools if they are available: list job templates and workflow job templates and confirm that 'Lightwell | Application Patch Pipeline' exists in organization Default. Also list inventories and note Demo Inventory.
3. Decide a single route:
   - apply_now: lightwell_patch_available is true AND the app environment is not production (staging/dev/build can auto-apply)
   - approved_patch: lightwell_patch_available is true AND the app is production (human approval required)
   - investigate: lightwell_patch_available is false, the app is not in the SBOM estate, or the package cannot be identified

If environment is not stated, treat payments-api as staging and checkout-service as production.

The JSON MUST have a top-level key named route. Do not wrap the object in final or any other key.

Output ONLY valid JSON:
{
  "route": "apply_now or approved_patch or investigate",
  "advisory_id": "",
  "cve_id": "",
  "severity": "",
  "package_name": "",
  "patched_version": "",
  "affected_app": "",
  "environment": "",
  "lightwell_patch_available": false,
  "aap_workflow_name": "Lightwell | Application Patch Pipeline",
  "confidence": 0.0,
  "reasoning": "one or two sentences"
}

cases.label: Auto-apply (non-prod)
cases.condition: ('route' in ${analyze_agent.result.content} and ${analyze_agent.result.content.route} == 'apply_now') or ('final' in ${analyze_agent.result.content} and (${analyze_agent.result.content.final} == 'apply_now' or 'apply_now' in ${analyze_agent.result.content.final}))

cases.label: Approval required (prod)
cases.condition: ('route' in ${analyze_agent.result.content} and ${analyze_agent.result.content.route} == 'approved_patch') or ('final' in ${analyze_agent.result.content} and (${analyze_agent.result.content.final} == 'approved_patch' or 'approved_patch' in ${analyze_agent.result.content.final}))

cases.label: Investigate
cases.condition: ('route' in ${analyze_agent.result.content} and ${analyze_agent.result.content.route} == 'investigate') or ('final' in ${analyze_agent.result.content} and (${analyze_agent.result.content.final} == 'investigate' or 'investigate' in ${analyze_agent.result.content.final}))

extra_vars.recommended_action: Operator rejected the production Lightwell patch. Application stays on the vulnerable dependency.
Analyze agent did not return apply_now, approved_patch, or investigate.
